description: Canonical chess motif taxonomy — the weakness-category vocabulary the RSI loop targets, and the detector roadmap. `category` is tactical (board-scan detector) | mate (post-mate pattern classifier) | positional. `family` groups related motifs; `parent` (when present) names the broader motif a subtype belongs to. `detectedBy` names the engine component that recognizes the motif today; `detectedBy: null` is a DETECTION GAP — an item on the build roadmap. Tactical, mate, and positional definitions follow ChessTempo's authoritative tagging definitions (chesstempo.com/tactical-motifs and chesstempo.com/positional-motifs).
sources: chesstempo.com/tactical-motifs — authoritative tactical + checkmate definitions (provided verbatim by the user; use these over other definitions per ChessTempo's tagging guideline)

chesstempo.com/positional-motifs — authoritative positional definitions (provided verbatim by the user); the positional set below has been reconciled and expanded from ~59 ChessTempo positional motifs (plus a few taxonomy-specific entries ChessTempo omits: hanging-pawns, pawn-island, weak-square, color-complex, fianchetto).

motifs.name: Double Attack
motifs.definition: One move creates two or more threats at once.

motifs.name: Fork
motifs.definition: A single piece attacks two or more targets simultaneously.

motifs.name: Family Fork
motifs.definition: A knight fork hitting the king plus several major/minor pieces at once.

motifs.name: Royal Fork
motifs.definition: A fork that hits both the enemy king and queen.

motifs.name: Pawn Fork
motifs.definition: A pawn attacks two pieces at once.

motifs.name: Tag Team
motifs.definition: Two pieces alternate threats the opponent cannot meet together.

motifs.name: Absolute Pin
motifs.definition: A piece pinned to its king (illegal to move).

motifs.name: Relative Pin
motifs.definition: A piece pinned to a more valuable piece behind it.

motifs.name: Cross-pin
motifs.definition: A piece pinned along two lines at once.

motifs.name: Mate Pin
motifs.definition: A pin that enables or is part of a mate.

motifs.name: Unpinning
motifs.definition: Breaking a pin (e.g. by interposing or counterattacking the pinner).

motifs.name: Skewer
motifs.definition: Attack a valuable piece on a line so that moving it exposes a lesser piece behind.

motifs.name: Relative Skewer
motifs.definition: A skewer where the front piece is more valuable than the one behind, but not the king.

motifs.name: Skewer of Queen
motifs.definition: The skewered (front) piece is the queen.

motifs.name: Skewer of Rook
motifs.definition: The skewered (front) piece is a rook.

motifs.name: Skewer of King
motifs.definition: The king is forced to move off the line, winning the piece behind it.

motifs.name: X-Ray Attack
motifs.definition: A slider attacks through an enemy piece to a target behind it.

motifs.name: X-Ray Defense
motifs.definition: A slider defends a friendly piece through an enemy piece.

motifs.name: Discovered Attack
motifs.definition: Moving a piece unveils an attack from a piece behind it.

motifs.name: Discovered Check
motifs.definition: A discovered attack where the unveiled piece gives check.

motifs.name: Discoverer Checks
motifs.definition: A discovered attack where the MOVING piece gives check.

motifs.name: Double Check
motifs.definition: Both the moving piece and the unveiled piece check the king; the king must move.

motifs.name: Discovered Defense
motifs.definition: Moving a piece unveils a defense of a friendly piece/square behind it.

motifs.name: Removing the Guard
motifs.definition: Eliminate or neutralize the piece guarding a key target.

motifs.name: Capturing the Defender
motifs.definition: Capture the defender of a target.

motifs.name: Distraction
motifs.definition: Force a defender away by giving it a more urgent duty.

motifs.name: Attacking the Defender
motifs.definition: Attack the defender so it must move or be lost.

motifs.name: Luring the Defender
motifs.definition: Entice a defender off its post (decoy a defender).

motifs.name: Overloading
motifs.definition: A defender tasked with too many duties is exploited.

motifs.name: Interference
motifs.definition: Interpose to cut the defensive connection between two enemy pieces.

motifs.name: Attraction
motifs.definition: Pull an enemy piece to a bad square, usually via an active sacrifice (decoy-toward).

motifs.name: Coercion
motifs.definition: Force a piece to a bad square via a direct attack or passive sacrifice (push, not pull).

motifs.name: Blocking
motifs.definition: Force an enemy piece onto a square, removing it as an escape square for another piece.

motifs.name: Controlling Escape Square
motifs.definition: Cover an enemy piece's escape square so it can be trapped/mated.

motifs.name: Clearance
motifs.definition: Vacate a square or line for another friendly piece.

motifs.name: Diagonal Clearance
motifs.definition: Clear a piece off a diagonal for another piece to use it.

motifs.name: File Clearance
motifs.definition: Clear a piece off a file for another piece to use it.

motifs.name: Rank Clearance
motifs.definition: Clear a piece off a rank for another piece to use it.

motifs.name: Square Clearance
motifs.definition: Move a piece off a square so another friendly piece can use it.

motifs.name: Counting
motifs.definition: Win material by counting attackers vs defenders across an exchange sequence.

motifs.name: Under-protected Piece
motifs.definition: More attackers than defenders on one square forces material gain.

motifs.name: Multi-square Counting
motifs.definition: Forced material gain via captures across several squares.

motifs.name: Hanging Piece
motifs.definition: An undefended (or under-defended) piece can be won for free.

motifs.name: Trapped Piece
motifs.definition: A piece has no safe square and will be lost.

motifs.name: Domination
motifs.definition: A piece is lost despite nominally having squares — every escape is covered.

motifs.name: Win the Exchange
motifs.definition: Win a rook for a minor piece.

motifs.name: Hook and Ladder
motifs.definition: A trick where stacked major pieces win material via an in-between capture.

motifs.name: Simplification
motifs.definition: Trade pieces to reach a winning endgame.

motifs.name: Zwischenzug
motifs.definition: An in-between move (often a check) inserted before the expected reply.

motifs.name: Desperado
motifs.definition: An already-doomed piece grabs material or creates havoc before dying.

motifs.name: Hit and Run
motifs.definition: Capture/threaten then retreat to safety with tempo.

motifs.name: Capturing the Attacker
motifs.definition: Remove the attacking piece to defuse a threat with tempo.

motifs.name: Gain of Tempo
motifs.definition: A forcing move that gains time toward the goal.

motifs.name: Quiet Move
motifs.definition: A non-checking, non-capturing move that sets up an unstoppable threat.

motifs.name: Sacrifice
motifs.definition: Give up material for a larger gain.

motifs.name: Demolition Sacrifice
motifs.definition: Sacrifice to strip the king's pawn cover.

motifs.name: Greek Gift
motifs.definition: Bxh7+/Bxh2+ bishop sacrifice against the castled king.

motifs.name: Exchange Sacrifice
motifs.definition: Give up a rook for a minor piece for positional/attacking gain.

motifs.name: Passive Sacrifice
motifs.definition: Offer material that the opponent may decline.

motifs.name: Pawn Sacrifice
motifs.definition: Give up a pawn for initiative, lines, or tempo.

motifs.name: Unsound Sacrifice
motifs.definition: A sacrifice that is objectively incorrect (practical/swindle value only).

motifs.name: Advanced Pawn
motifs.definition: A pawn past the center participating meaningfully in the tactic.

motifs.name: Non-Promotion Advanced Pawn
motifs.definition: An advanced pawn that helps the tactic without promoting/threatening it.

motifs.name: Promotion
motifs.definition: The tactic requires promoting a pawn.

motifs.name: Underpromotion
motifs.definition: Promote to a non-queen for a fork, check, or to avoid stalemate.

motifs.name: Promotion Threat
motifs.definition: The threat to promote drives the tactic without promoting.

motifs.name: Underpromotion Threat
motifs.definition: A threatened underpromotion influences the outcome.

motifs.name: Pawn Breakthrough
motifs.definition: A pawn sacrifice that forces through an unstoppable passed pawn.

motifs.name: Weak Back Rank
motifs.definition: Exploit a king hemmed in on its back rank by its own pawns.

motifs.name: Exposed King
motifs.definition: An open/under-defended king enables the tactic.

motifs.name: Mate Threat
motifs.definition: A threatened forced mate constrains the opponent.

motifs.name: Counter Check
motifs.definition: Answer a check with a check (cross-check), often by interposing with check.

motifs.name: Windmill
motifs.definition: A repeating series of forced discovered checks harvesting material.

motifs.name: Windmill - Discoveries
motifs.definition: Windmill driven by discovered checks.

motifs.name: Windmill - Knight Fork
motifs.definition: Windmill driven by repeated knight-fork checks.

motifs.name: Defensive Move
motifs.definition: A serious threat must be met in the one correct way.

motifs.name: Defensive Interposition
motifs.definition: Block the line between an enemy attacker and your own piece/square.

motifs.name: Recapture
motifs.definition: Recapture correctly (the choice of recapturing piece is critical).

motifs.name: Avoiding Mate
motifs.definition: Meet a mate threat with the only saving move.

motifs.name: Avoiding Perpetual
motifs.definition: Play to prevent the opponent's perpetual check.

motifs.name: Avoiding Stalemate
motifs.definition: Win while avoiding stalemating the opponent.

motifs.name: Achieving Perpetual
motifs.definition: Save a bad position with a forced perpetual check.

motifs.name: En Passant
motifs.definition: An en-passant capture is required by the tactic.

motifs.name: Tactical Castling
motifs.definition: Castling used as a tactical resource (e.g. activating the rook with tempo).

motifs.name: Backwards Move
motifs.definition: A retreating move is the key, easily-missed resource.

motifs.name: Long Lateral Move
motifs.definition: A long sideways slider move is the key, easily-missed resource.

motifs.name: Battery
motifs.definition: Two pieces aligned on a file/rank/diagonal to multiply force.

motifs.name: Queen + Bishop Battery
motifs.definition: Queen and bishop doubled on the same diagonal.

motifs.name: Two Rooks Battery
motifs.definition: Two rooks doubled on a file or rank.

motifs.name: Alekhine's Gun
motifs.definition: Doubled rooks backed by the queen on the same file.

motifs.name: Zugzwang
motifs.definition: Any move worsens the opponent's position.

motifs.name: Triangulation
motifs.definition: Lose a tempo with the king to put the opponent in zugzwang.

motifs.name: Anastasia's Mate
motifs.definition: King trapped on the edge; rook/queen mates while a knight blocks escape.

motifs.name: Arabian Mate
motifs.definition: Rook + knight mate the king in the corner.

motifs.name: Hook Mate
motifs.definition: Rook mates protected by a knight, knight protected by a pawn, escape blocked.

motifs.name: Vukovic Mate
motifs.definition: Rook (supported) mates on the edge with a knight covering flight squares.

motifs.name: Back Rank Mate
motifs.definition: Mate on the back rank behind the king's own unmoved pawns.

motifs.name: Edge Mate
motifs.definition: Back-rank/side-file family mate with the king hemmed by its own pieces.

motifs.name: Side File Mate
motifs.definition: Back-rank-style mate on a side file.

motifs.name: Edge Pin Mate
motifs.definition: Back-rank/side-file mate exploiting a pin on a defender.

motifs.name: Queen Cutoff Mate
motifs.definition: Queen mates one square from the king on its edge, cutting the diagonal escape.

motifs.name: Smothered Mate
motifs.definition: Knight mates a king completely boxed in by its own pieces.

motifs.name: Suffocation Mate
motifs.definition: Knight mate where attacker pieces (not only friendly ones) cut off escape.

motifs.name: Epaulette Mate
motifs.definition: Queen/rook mate with the king's own pieces blocking the two parallel escapes.

motifs.name: Dovetail Mate
motifs.definition: Supported queen mates diagonally adjacent; the two escapes are self-blocked.

motifs.name: Dovetail Mate - Bishop
motifs.definition: Dovetail mate where the attacker's bishop blocks the escapes.

motifs.name: Swallow's Tail Mate
motifs.definition: Supported queen adjacent to the king; king's own rooks block the diagonals.

motifs.name: Damiano's Bishop Mate
motifs.definition: Queen mates on the edge protected by a bishop.

motifs.name: Damiano's Mate
motifs.definition: Pawn-supported queen mate with the king restricted on the back rank.

motifs.name: Lolli's Mate
motifs.definition: Pawn on the 6th supports a queen mate on the back rank.

motifs.name: Greco's Mate
motifs.definition: Queen/rook mates the king in the corner with a bishop covering the diagonal.

motifs.name: Balestra Mate
motifs.definition: Queen + bishop mate on intersecting diagonals; bishop delivers, queen blocks.

motifs.name: Escalator Mate
motifs.definition: Queen, supported by a bishop on the diagonal, walks the king to mate.

motifs.name: Morphy's Mate
motifs.definition: Bishop mates with a rook cutting horizontal escape and a pawn the vertical.

motifs.name: Boden's Mate
motifs.definition: Two bishops mate on intersecting diagonals; king blocked by its own pieces.

motifs.name: Double Bishop Mate
motifs.definition: Two bishops control adjacent diagonals to mate, escape blocked.

motifs.name: Blackburne's Mate
motifs.definition: Two bishops + knight mate on the edge with an enemy piece blocking escape.

motifs.name: Threading the Needle Mate
motifs.definition: Queen/bishop diagonal mate threaded between blocking pieces.

motifs.name: Opera Mate
motifs.definition: Rook on the edge next to the king, supported by a bishop on the diagonal.

motifs.name: Pillsbury's Mate
motifs.definition: Rook mates near the corner with a bishop blocking the corner escape.

motifs.name: Kill Box Mate
motifs.definition: Rook adjacent to the king + queen a diagonal step back form a 3×3 box.

motifs.name: Triangle Mate
motifs.definition: Queen mates supported by a parallel rook one square away (a triangle).

motifs.name: Lawnmower Mate
motifs.definition: Two major pieces ladder the king to the edge (a.k.a. ladder mate).

motifs.name: Railroad Mate
motifs.definition: Queen + rook a rank/file apart drive the king along the 'tracks' to mate.

motifs.name: Monorail Mate
motifs.definition: Queen + rook in adjacent ranks/files walk the king to mate.

motifs.name: Walking the Plank Mate
motifs.definition: Two majors with a one-file gap restrict the king to a 'plank', then mate.

motifs.name: Queen and Knight Mate
motifs.definition: Queen and knight coordinate to mate.

motifs.name: Pawn Mate
motifs.definition: Mate delivered by a pawn.

motifs.name: Promotion Mate
motifs.definition: Mate delivered by a promoted pawn (incl. underpromotion mate).

motifs.name: Discovered Mate
motifs.definition: Mate delivered via a discovered check.

motifs.name: Double Checkmate
motifs.definition: Mate where both the discoverer and the discovered piece check.

motifs.name: Counter Check Checkmate
motifs.definition: A discovery that mates while interposing against a check on your own king.

motifs.name: X-Ray Mate
motifs.definition: Mate where a piece is x-ray-defended through the enemy king's lines.

motifs.name: Seizing a Square Mate
motifs.definition: Sacrifice to seize a defended square, then mate from/with it.

motifs.name: Isolated Pawn
motifs.definition: An isolated pawn has no friendly pawns on either adjacent file, so no pawn can defend it.

motifs.name: Doubled Pawns
motifs.definition: Two pawns of the same colour on the same file.

motifs.name: Backward Pawn
motifs.definition: A pawn on a half-open file that cannot be protected by a pawn on either side (its neighbours have advanced past it) and cannot safely advance.

motifs.name: Passed Pawn
motifs.definition: A pawn that no enemy pawn can stop from progressing to the promotion square.

motifs.name: Protected Passed Pawn
motifs.definition: A passed pawn defended by another friendly pawn.

motifs.name: Outside Passed Pawn
motifs.definition: A passed pawn far from the other pawns, often a decisive decoy in the endgame.

motifs.name: Connected Pawns
motifs.definition: Two or more pawns of the same colour on adjacent files, able to defend one another.

motifs.name: Pawn Phalanx
motifs.definition: Two or more adjacent pawns of the same colour abreast on the same rank.

motifs.name: Pawn Majority
motifs.definition: More pawns than the opponent on one section of the board.

motifs.name: Hanging Pawns
motifs.definition: Two adjacent friendly pawns on a half-open file with no pawn support, both potential targets.

motifs.name: Pawn Islands
motifs.definition: Groups of connected pawns separated by files with no friendly pawns.

motifs.name: Pawn Break
motifs.definition: A pawn advance that challenges the opponent's structure or centre to gain space, counterplay, or a passed pawn.

motifs.name: Pawn Storm
motifs.definition: A rapid advance of connected pawns down the board, typically against the castled king.

motifs.name: Minority Attack
motifs.definition: Advancing a pawn minority against the opponent's pawn majority to create a lasting weakness.

motifs.name: Pawn Grab
motifs.definition: Capturing a pawn while conceding significant positional compensation.

motifs.name: Pawn Blockade
motifs.definition: Halting a pawn's advance by planting a piece or pawn directly in front of it.

motifs.name: Knight Outpost
motifs.definition: A square in the opponent's half, safe from enemy pawns and usually pawn-protected, ideal for a knight.

motifs.name: Good Knight / Outpost Knight
motifs.definition: A knight established on a strong, supported, unassailable square.

motifs.name: Weak Square
motifs.definition: A square that can no longer be defended by a pawn.

motifs.name: Color Complex Weakness
motifs.definition: A chronic weakness on the squares of one colour.

motifs.name: Bishop Pair
motifs.definition: Holding both bishops against bishop+knight or two knights, a significant edge in open positions.

motifs.name: Bad Bishop
motifs.definition: A bishop whose activity is restricted by its own pawns and pieces, especially fixed pawns on its own colour.

motifs.name: Good Bishop
motifs.definition: A bishop whose diagonals are not blocked by its own pawns, which sit mostly on the opposite colour.

motifs.name: Opposite Colour Bishops
motifs.definition: Each side has a single bishop, on different square colours; often drawish in the endgame.

motifs.name: Same Colour Bishops
motifs.definition: Each side has a single bishop of the same square colour, often key in endgame analysis.

motifs.name: Improve Piece Activity
motifs.definition: A move that increases the number of squares a piece influences.

motifs.name: Limit Piece Activity
motifs.definition: A move that restricts an opponent piece's influence, e.g. blocking a bishop's diagonal.

motifs.name: Piece Coordination
motifs.definition: Pieces placed so they co-operate effectively toward a common goal.

motifs.name: Queen + Knight Coordination
motifs.definition: Queen and knight working together, often to attack the enemy king.

motifs.name: Piece Centralisation
motifs.definition: Moving a piece toward the centre to increase its control of the board.

motifs.name: Centralised King
motifs.definition: In the endgame, a king placed in the centre to coordinate with its pieces and support pawns.

motifs.name: Open File
motifs.definition: A file with no pawns of either colour, a highway for rooks.

motifs.name: Closed File
motifs.definition: A file blocked by a non-passed pawn of each colour, restricting rook activity.

motifs.name: Semi-Open File
motifs.definition: A file with only one side's pawn; semi-open (half-open) at the end missing a pawn.

motifs.name: File Control
motifs.definition: Control of an open or semi-open file by a rook or queen.

motifs.name: Rank Control
motifs.definition: Control of a rank by a rook or queen, e.g. cutting off the enemy king.

motifs.name: Diagonal Control
motifs.definition: Control of a diagonal by a bishop or queen.

motifs.name: Rook on the 7th
motifs.definition: A rook penetrated to the 7th rank, attacking pawns and confining the king.

motifs.name: Rook Lift
motifs.definition: Lifting a rook off the back rank to swing it along a rank into an attack.

motifs.name: Connected Rooks
motifs.definition: Two friendly rooks with no piece between them, giving mutual protection.

motifs.name: Doubled Rooks
motifs.definition: Two friendly rooks connected on the same file (a two-piece vertical battery).

motifs.name: Penetration
motifs.definition: The entry of a piece deep into the enemy position, e.g. a rook reaching the 7th rank.

motifs.name: Diagonal Battery
motifs.definition: Two or more diagonal-moving pieces (bishops/queen) stacked on one diagonal as a joint attacking force.

motifs.name: Vertical Battery
motifs.definition: Multiple pieces (rooks/queen) stacked on the same file as a joint force; Alekhine's Gun and doubled rooks are specific cases.

motifs.name: King Safety
motifs.definition: How exposed the king is to attack, e.g. a disrupted pawn shield or imminent threats.

motifs.name: King March
motifs.definition: A series of king moves toward a goal: escaping checks, dodging a mating net, or aiding its army.

motifs.name: Luft
motifs.definition: Creating an escape square for the king (usually a pawn move) to avoid back-rank mate.

motifs.name: Opposite Side Castling
motifs.definition: One side castles kingside and the other queenside, often leading to mutual pawn-storm attacks.

motifs.name: Space
motifs.definition: Controlling more territory than the opponent, cramping their pieces.

motifs.name: Center Control
motifs.definition: Control of the central squares, giving superior mobility across the board.

motifs.name: Opening the Centre
motifs.definition: Exchanging pawns or pieces to open the centre and activate one's better-placed pieces.

motifs.name: Prophylaxis
motifs.definition: Play aimed at preventing the opponent's intended actions before pursuing one's own.

motifs.name: Overprotection
motifs.definition: A form of prophylaxis: defending a key point more than currently needed, freeing the defenders.

motifs.name: Defence
motifs.definition: A move that defends a piece, a square, or against an enemy threat.

motifs.name: Initiative
motifs.definition: Holding the initiative: being the side most able to make threats.

motifs.name: Avoid Trade
motifs.definition: Declining a trade that would lead to a positional disadvantage.

motifs.name: Favourable Trade
motifs.definition: A trade of pieces that improves one's position.

motifs.name: Positional Sacrifice - Exchange
motifs.definition: Giving up a rook for a minor piece in return for positional compensation.

motifs.name: Positional Sacrifice - Pawn
motifs.definition: Sacrificing a pawn for positional compensation.

motifs.name: Positional Sacrifice - Piece
motifs.definition: Sacrificing a minor piece for positional compensation.

motifs.name: Positional Sacrifice - Queen
motifs.definition: Sacrificing the queen for positional (and often partial material) compensation.

motifs.name: Positional Sacrifice - Rook
motifs.definition: Sacrificing a rook for positional (and often partial material) compensation.

motifs.name: Fianchetto
motifs.definition: Developing a bishop to the long diagonal behind a g- or b-pawn.
